annotations.title: Virgins.
annotations.text: These virgins fiue wise, and fiue foolish, signifie that in the Church militant there be good and bad: which bad shal be shut out at the later day, although they haue lampes (that is faith) as the other, ◦ because their lampes are out, that is, their faith is dead without charity and good workes to lighten them Greg. ho. 12.

annotations.title: Lampes.
annotations.text: These lampes lighted, be good workes, namely of mercy, and the laudable conuersation which shineth before men. Aug. ep. 120, c. 33.

annotations.title: Oyle.
annotations.text: ◦ This oyle is the right inward intention directing our workes to Gods glorie, and not to the praise of our selues in the sight of men. Aug. ep. 120, c. 33.

annotations.title: With vsurie.
annotations.text: Vsurie is here taken for the lawful gaine that a man getteth by wel employing his goods. When God geueth vs any talent or talents, he looketh for vsurie, that is, for spiritual increase of the same by our diligence and industrie.

annotations.title: That which he seemeth to haue.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> He is said to haue Gods gifts, that vseth them, and to such an one God wil increase his giftes. He that vseth them not, seemeth to haue, rather then hath them. and from him God wil withdraw that which before he gaue.

annotations.title: Separate.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Lo here is the separation, for in the Church militant they liued both together. As for Heretikes, they went out of the Church before, and separated them selues, and therfore are not to be separated here, as being iudged already.

notes.text: Good and bad in the Church.

annotations.title: Come ye, 41 get ye away.
annotations.text: ◦ It is no incongruity that God should say, Goe into euerlasting fire, to them that by their free wil haue repelled his mercie: and to the other, Come ye blessed of my father, take the kingdom prepared for them, that by their free wil haue receiued faith, and confessed their sinnes and done penance. Aug. li. 2 act. cum Fel. Manich. c. 8.

notes.text: Heauen is the reward of good workes, and Hel of the contrarie.

annotations.title: You gaue me.
annotations.text: Hereby we see how much almes-deedes and al workes of mercy preuaile towardes life euerlasting, and to blot out former sinnes. Aug. in Ps. 49.

annotations.title: Gaue me not.
annotations.text: He chargeth them not here that they beleeued not, but that they did not good workes. For such did beleeue, but they cared not for good workes, as though by dead faith they might haue come to heauen. Aug. de fid. & op. c. 15. & ad Dulcit. q. 2. to. 4.
